access: Vaile Mansion is a museum run by the Victorian Society of the Vaile Mansion; tours (adults about $10) Thursday to Saturday 10 to 4 and Sunday 1 to 4, April 1 to October 31, plus holiday tours late Nov to Dec 22. No source states whether the grounds can be walked outside tour hours or without a ticket; confirm on 816-503-6700 before promising it. MDC lists public access YES. Independence is about 16 km east of downtown Kansas City.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its size: a smoketree 12.5 metres tall with a crown 11.9 metres wide, in a species that usually stays small. It stands on the Vaile Mansion grounds; ask at the mansion which one.
verify_notes: MDC champion layer: Cotinus obovatus, Jackson County, circumference 95 in (241 cm), height 41 ft (12.5 m), spread 39 ft (11.9 m), Missouri points as listed, not a national champion, owner City of Independence (the layer says City of Independence; the Vaile Society manages the museum). Points are fuzzed to site level. City of Independence heritage layer (same tree, category LEG, location 1500 N Liberty St, point 39.10733,-94.41679, approved 2026; Date_Planted field carries a value that reads as c.1915 but is probably a placeholder, NOT used as an age). No age source: age left empty, page should ask the reader. Girth sanity: 241 cm is large for a smoketree, which is normally a small multi-stemmed tree (MBG: 20 to 30 ft); a multi-stem measurement at 4.5 ft is likely, unverified. Alive: the 2023 JCHS essay and the ArbNet page (about a year old) both name it as present; no dated photo seen; lifecheck NONE. Flagged: register-only plus two soft descriptions, aliveness thin, exact tree not identified on the grounds, grounds access outside tours unstated. Independence, not Kansas City proper; label with its real place. Paid share: this is a ticketed site. Also on the grounds, from the same sources: a Liberty elm from the Elm Research Institute and an allee of 30 sugar maples in two rows of 15 north of the mansion (no measurements, planting dates unsourced).
story:
American smoketrees are supposed to stay small. This one is Missouri's largest, 12.5 metres tall on the grounds of the Vaile Mansion in Independence.

The Missouri Department of Conservation's champion register gives it a trunk 2.41 metres round, 95 inches, under a crown 11.9 metres across. The species is normally a small, often multi-stemmed tree, six to nine metres at most by the Missouri Botanical Garden's account, so this is a great deal of smoketree. The girth may have been taken around several stems at once. No source says, so read it as the register's number rather than proof of one solid trunk.

It grows on the five acres around the Vaile Mansion, a Gilded Age house that is now a museum and an accredited arboretum. Its neighbours there include a Liberty elm from the Elm Research Institute and an avenue of 30 sugar maples in two rows north of the house. In 2026 the City of Independence added the smoketree to its own heritage tree list as well.

Now the honest part. No source we found says exactly where on the grounds it stands, and the latest written mentions are a 2023 historical society essay and the arboretum's listing, so ask at the mansion which tree it is. The house is open for paid tours from April to October and again before Christmas. Nobody has published the tree's age either. If you know when it was planted, tell us.
